record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Fix an ergodic measure-preserving transformation T0 on a standard probability space (X, μ), and let [T0] be its full group, consisting of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X that send each point to another point in its T0-orbit. If T1 and T2 are Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy and the same orbits as T0, does there exist T ∈ [T0] such that T1 = T T2 T^{-1}?

evidence.quote: Let us first fix an ergodic transformation T0, and define its full group [T0] as the group of bimeasurable bijections U : X → X such that for all x, the point U(x) belongs to the T0-orbit of x.
Question 4.2 (Thouvenot). Let T1, T2 be two Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy, suppose that they have the same orbits as T0. Is there T ∈ [T0] such that T1 = T T2T−1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mu)$ be a standard probability space and let $T_0 : X \to X$ be an ergodic measure-preserving automorphism. The full group of $T_0$ is
$$[T_0] = \{U : X \to X \text{ bimeasurable bijection} : U(x) \in \{T_0^n x : n \in \mathbb{Z}\} \text{ for $\mu$-a.e. } x\}.$$
Suppose $T_1$ and $T_2$ are two Bernoulli shifts on $(X,\mu)$ that have the same Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy and such that, for $\mu$-a.e. $x \in X$, the $T_1$-orbit, the $T_2$-orbit and the $T_0$-orbit of $x$ all coincide. Must there exist $T \in [T_0]$ such that
$$T_1 = T\, T_2\, T^{-1}\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question of Thouvenot about conjugating equal-entropy Bernoulli shifts having the same orbits via an element of the full group of an ambient ergodic transformation. Related results on orbit equivalence and isomorphism of Bernoulli shifts exist, but none directly answer this question, so its status appears unknown/open.

status_evidence.title: Bernoulli shifts with bases of equal entropy are isomorphic
status_evidence.snippet: Equal-entropy Bernoulli shifts are isomorphic, but this does not address conjugation within a full group preserving orbits.
status_evidence.claim: Related Bernoulli isomorphism results do not settle the full-group conjugacy question.
